Standard: The drag or spin chute design, attachments, and deployments meet all specified performance requirements without causing adverse loading or damage to the air vehicle. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Review of flight manual verifies air vehicle speeds for deployment and drag performance of the chute are available to the flight crew and information aligns with qualified design. Analysis.
  (1) Conduct sizing analysis to verify the drag chute aids in decelerating the air vehicle to meet stopping distance requirements and required runway conditions (e.g., dry, wet and icy surfaces).
  (2) Conduct sizing analysis to verify the spin chute stabilizes the air vehicle to recover from a spin in flight.
  (3) Conduct loads analysis to determine shock and sustained loads from chute deployment.
  (4) Conduct static strength stress analysis of chute mechanisms, landing gear and air vehicle structure to verify various components are sized for the chute loads. Gross section yielding or detrimental deformations do not occur at or below 115% DLL. No chute panel blow out, rupture of structure and risers, premature release of chute occurs at or below ultimate loads. Ultimate load is 1.5X DLL.
  (5) Conduct trajectory analysis to show that chute canopy and lines deployment minimizes contact with the air vehicle to allow full deployment of chute. Test.
    (1) Ground test: Conduct testing on air vehicle to verify the installation, functionality, and performance capability of the drag or spin chute system. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Test.
    (2) Flight test: Conduct testing on air vehicle to verify the installation, functionality, and performance capability of the drag chute system during flight, approaches, landings, and RTOs.
